description: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy of various probing methods applied to multilingual BERT models, as presented in the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models.” The vertical axis represents accuracy, ranging from 70 to 95 in increments of 5, while the horizontal axis lists different probing configurations grouped into three main categories: “1st layer,” “random layers,” and “random,” each with subvariants including “+B₂,” “+L₂,” “+R₂,” and “+permute,” plus an “unperturbed” baseline. The bars are color-coded: light blue and dark blue for “1st layer” variants (accuracy ~80–82), light green and dark green for “random layers” variants (~79–82), light pink and red for “random” variants (~71–73), and orange for the “unperturbed” condition (~90–92). The “unperturbed” bar is notably taller than all others, indicating significantly higher accuracy. Within each group, the second bar (e.g., dark blue, dark green, red) is consistently taller than the first (light blue, light green, pink), suggesting that the second variant in each pair performs better. The chart visually emphasizes the performance gap between perturbed probing methods and the unperturbed baseline, with the latter achieving near 92% accuracy, while most perturbed conditions fall between 71% and 82%.
